final_note: You worked through Moments, levers and gears (physics only) — 12 specification statements.

concepts.def: A force, or a system of forces, may cause an object to rotate rather than to move along a straight line. Rotation happens when the line of action of the force does not pass through the fixed point about which the object can turn, so the force acts at some perpendicular distance from that point.

The fixed point about which an object turns. Moments are always stated about a particular pivot: the same force can have a large moment about one pivot and no moment at all about another, because the perpendicular distance is different in each case.

The turning effect of a force is called the moment of the force. It is a measure of how strongly a force tends to turn an object about a pivot, and it depends on both the size of the force and its perpendicular distance from the pivot.

The size of the moment is defined by the equation: moment of a force = force × distance, written in symbols as M = F d. Both quantities on the right multiply, so doubling either the force or the distance doubles the moment.

concepts.term: Quantities and units in M = F d
concepts.def: Moment of a force, M, is in newton-metres, Nm. Force, F, is in newtons, N. Distance, d, is in metres, m. A force given as a mass in kilograms must first be converted to a weight in newtons, and a distance given in centimetres or millimetres must be converted to metres before the equation is used.

In M = F d, the distance d is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force, measured in metres. It is not necessarily the length of the bar, nor the distance along the object to the point of contact; when the force is at an angle to the object, the perpendicular distance is shorter than that.

concepts.term: Line of action of a force
concepts.def: The straight line through the point where the force acts, drawn along the direction in which the force acts and extended in both directions. The perpendicular distance d is measured from the pivot to this line. If the line of action passes through the pivot, d is zero and the moment is zero.

Each force acting on an object turns it about the pivot in one of two senses. A moment that would turn the object clockwise is a clockwise moment; one that would turn it anticlockwise is an anticlockwise moment. Where several forces act in the same sense, their moments are added to give the total moment in that sense.

If an object is balanced, the total clockwise moment about a pivot equals the total anticlockwise moment about that pivot. Balance is a statement about moments, not about the forces themselves: a small force far from the pivot can balance a large force close to it.

concepts.term: Finding an unknown force or distance
concepts.def: For an object that is balanced, set the total clockwise moment equal to the total anticlockwise moment and solve for the unknown. Work out every known moment as force × distance first, then rearrange M = F d as F = M ÷ d to find a force, or d = M ÷ F to find a distance from the pivot.

A simple lever is a rigid bar that turns about a pivot and is used to transmit the rotational effect of a force. An effort applied at a large distance from the pivot produces a large moment, and that same moment can move a much larger load acting at a small distance from the pivot, so the lever acts as a force multiplier.

A simple gear system is a set of toothed wheels that mesh together and transmit the rotational effect of a force from one wheel to the next. Meshed gears turn in opposite directions. When a small gear drives a larger one, the larger gear turns more slowly but the force at the teeth acts at a greater distance from its axle, so it exerts a larger moment.

Everyday examples include pushing a door open at the handle so it swings about its hinges, pulling a spanner to turn a nut, pushing down on a bicycle pedal to turn the crank about the axle, turning a steering wheel, using a crowbar to lever up a lid, and a see-saw tipping when a child sits on one end. In each case the force acts at a perpendicular distance from a pivot.

mcqs.q: In which of these situations does the force described make the object rotate?
options: A push on the edge of a door, away from its hinges
A push on a door aimed straight through its hinges
Two equal pushes on opposite faces of a still box
A ball falling straight down under its own weight
mcqs.explain: The line of action of the push is at a perpendicular distance from the hinge, so the force has a moment about the hinge and the door swings.

mcqs.q: A cyclist pushes vertically down on one pedal. Which statement best describes what this single force does?
options: It cannot turn the crank because it is only one force
It turns the crank only when it acts through the axle
Its moment is measured in newtons at the pedal itself
It has a turning effect on the pedal crank about the axle
mcqs.explain: The push acts at a perpendicular distance from the axle, so it has a moment about the axle and turns the crank.

mcqs.q: A force acts on a bar that can turn about a pivot. What is the turning effect of that force called?
options: Its moment about that pivot
Its resultant force at the pivot
Its lever arm from the pivot
The work it does at the pivot
mcqs.explain: The specification states that the turning effect of a force is called the moment of the force.

mcqs.q: The size of the moment of a force is defined by which equation?
options: moment of a force = force ÷ distance
moment of a force = force × bar length
moment of a force = force × distance
moment of a force = distance ÷ force
mcqs.explain: This is the equation exactly as the specification defines it, written in symbols as M = F d.

mcqs.q: Which row gives the correct units to use in M = F d?
options: M in Nm, F in N, d in cm
M in Nm, F in N, d in m
M in Nm, F in kg, d in m
M in N, F in N, d in m
mcqs.explain: The specification gives the moment in newton-metres, the force in newtons and the distance in metres.

mcqs.q: In the equation M = F d, what exactly does the distance d mean?
options: The distance from the pivot to the point where the force acts
The perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action
The distance the object moves as the force turns it round
The whole length of the bar or handle the force acts on
mcqs.explain: This is the specification's definition: the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force, in metres.

mcqs.q: A spanner is 0.30 m long. A 50 N force is applied at its end, but at an angle, so the perpendicular distance from the nut to the line of action of the force is 0.24 m. What is the moment about the nut?
options: 12 Nm
15 Nm
208 Nm
27 Nm
mcqs.explain: M = F d = 50 N × 0.24 m = 12 Nm, using the perpendicular distance to the line of action.

mcqs.q: A force of 25 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 0.20 m from a pivot. What is the moment of the force about the pivot?
options: 125 Nm
5.0 Nm
mcqs.explain: M = F d = 25 N × 0.20 m = 5.0 Nm, in newton-metres.

mcqs.q: A force of 40 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 15 cm from a pivot. What is the moment of the force?
options: 6.0 Nm
600 Nm
2.7 Nm
0.6 Nm

mcqs.q: An object is balanced about a pivot. Which statement must be true?
options: The total clockwise moment equals the total anticlockwise moment
The biggest force on one side matches the biggest on the other
The pivot must be at the exact centre of the balanced object
The forces on the two sides of the pivot are equal in size
mcqs.explain: This is the specification's condition for a balanced object, stated about the same pivot.

mcqs.q: A beam is balanced on a pivot. A 300 N weight hangs 1.2 m to the left of the pivot, and a single weight hangs 0.8 m to the right. What is the weight on the right?
mcqs.explain: Anticlockwise moment = 300 × 1.2 = 360 Nm, so the right-hand weight = 360 ÷ 0.8 = 450 N.

mcqs.q: A rod is balanced on a pivot. A 6.0 N force acts 0.50 m from the pivot on one side. A 4.0 N force acts on the other side. How far from the pivot is the 4.0 N force?
mcqs.explain: Moment on the first side = 6.0 × 0.50 = 3.0 Nm, so d = 3.0 ÷ 4.0 = 0.75 m.

mcqs.q: A rule balances with a 2 N weight 30 cm to the left of the pivot and a 3 N weight 20 cm to the right. The 2 N weight is replaced by a 3 N weight in the same place. Which single change will rebalance the rule?
options: Move the 3 N weight on the left to 45 cm from the pivot
Leave both weights as they are: the forces now match
Move the 3 N weight on the right to 10 cm from the pivot
Move the 3 N weight on the left to 20 cm from the pivot
mcqs.explain: The right-hand moment is 3 × 0.20 = 0.6 Nm, so the left-hand weight must also sit at 0.20 m to give 0.6 Nm.

mcqs.q: What do a simple lever and a simple gear system have in common?
options: Both create extra energy to make a bigger turning effect
Both are used to transmit the rotational effects of forces
Both turn a rotation into a straight-line push instead
Both need two forces before any rotation can happen
mcqs.explain: This is exactly what the specification says about a simple lever and a simple gear system.

mcqs.q: A gardener pushes down on the far end of a long spade handle to lever up a lump of soil. Why does this make the job easier?
options: The longer handle makes the pushing force itself become larger
The lever gives out a bigger moment than the one put into it
The longer handle makes the soil being lifted weigh less
The force acts further from the pivot, so its moment is larger
mcqs.explain: Because M = F d, the same push applied at a greater perpendicular distance from the pivot gives a larger moment.

mcqs.q: Two gear wheels are meshed together. The first gear is turned clockwise. How does the second gear turn?
options: It stays still until the first gear has turned fully around
Clockwise, as the turning effect is passed straight along
Anticlockwise, as their teeth push each other the other way
Clockwise, and at the same rate whatever their sizes are
mcqs.explain: At the meshing point the teeth of one gear drive the teeth of the other in the opposite sense, so directly meshed gears rotate opposite ways.

mcqs.q: A small gear drives a larger gear meshed with it. Compared with the small gear, the larger gear turns:
options: more quickly, and with a larger moment
more slowly, and with a smaller moment
more quickly, and with a smaller moment
more slowly, and with a larger moment
mcqs.explain: The larger gear has more teeth to move for one turn, so it rotates more slowly, but the tooth force acts further from its axle, so M = F d is larger.

mcqs.q: A force of 60 N is applied to a door along a line of action that passes exactly through the hinge. What is the moment of this force about the hinge?
options: 60 Nm, because a force that large must turn the door somehow
60 N, because the moment is just the force that is applied
60 N times the width of the door, measured from the hinge
Zero, because the perpendicular distance from the hinge is zero
mcqs.explain: The line of action passes through the pivot, so d = 0 and M = 60 × 0 = 0 Nm, however large the force.

mcqs.q: A 2.0 kg bag hangs from a beam at a perpendicular distance of 0.30 m from the pivot. Gravitational field strength is 9.8 N/kg. What is the moment of the bag's weight about the pivot?
options: 588 Nm
5.9 Nm
65 Nm
mcqs.explain: Weight = 2.0 × 9.8 = 19.6 N, so M = 19.6 × 0.30 = 5.88 Nm, which is 5.9 Nm to two significant figures.

mcqs.q: A plank pivots at its centre. On the left, a 10 N weight sits 0.40 m from the pivot and a 20 N weight sits 0.20 m from it. A single weight placed 0.50 m to the right balances the plank. What is that weight?
mcqs.explain: Total anticlockwise moment = (10 × 0.40) + (20 × 0.20) = 8.0 Nm, so the weight = 8.0 ÷ 0.50 = 16 N.
